exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Domain of a Transformed Square Root Function

question.explanation:
The domain of $y = \sqrt{x}$ is \[ x \ge 0. \]

To find the domain of $f(x) = 4\sqrt{7+x}+1,$ we replace $x$ with $7+x$ in the above inequality. This gives \[ {7+x} \ge 0. \]

Solving this inequality, we get \begin{align*} 7+x &\geq 0 \\[5pt] x &\geq -7 . \end{align*}

Therefore, the domain of $y=f(x)$ is $x \in \left[\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\textrm{$-7$}}, \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\textrm{$\infty$}}\right).$

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown below.

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Range of a Transformed Square Root Function

question.explanation:
The range of $\sqrt x$ is

\[ \sqrt x \ge 0. \]

Horizontal shifts and stretches do not affect the range. Hence,

\[ \sqrt{5x+9} \ge 0. \]

Multiplying the above inequality by $3,$ we get

\begin{align*} \sqrt{5x+9} &\ge 0 \\[3pt] 3\sqrt{5x+9} &\ge 0. \end{align*}

Therefore, the range of the given function is $f(x) \in [0,\infty).$

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown below.

example.title: Finding the Range of a Transformed Square Root Function

question.explanation:
The range of $\sqrt x$ is

\[ \sqrt x \ge 0. \]

Horizontal shifts do not affect the range. Hence,

\[ \sqrt{x-3} \ge 0. \]

Multiplying the above inequality by $\dfrac{3}{5}$ and then adding $3,$ we get

\begin{align*} \sqrt{x-3} &\ge 0 \\[3pt] \dfrac{3}{5}\sqrt{x-3} &\ge 0 \\[3pt] \dfrac{3}{5}\sqrt{x-3}+3 &\ge 3\\[3pt] f(x) & \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\ge} \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{3}. \end{align*}

Therefore, the range of the given function is $f(x) \in \left[3, \infty\right).$

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown below.

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Roots of a Transformed Square Root Function

question.explanation:
To find the root of $f(x),$ we must solve $f(x)=0\mathbin{:}$ \[ \sqrt{3x+1} + 4 = 0 \]

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

\begin{align*} \sqrt{3x+1} + 4 & = 0 \\[3pt] \sqrt{3x+1} & = -4\\[3pt] \end{align*}

This equation does not have any solutions since its left-hand side is always nonnegative, while the right-hand side is negative.

Therefore, $f(x)$ has no roots.

question.text: The root of the function $f(x) = - \sqrt{8-2x} +4$ is $x =$
question.explanation:
To find the root of $f(x),$ we must solve $f(x)=0{:}$ \[ - \sqrt{8-2x} +4 = 0 \]

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

\begin{align*} - \sqrt{8-2x} +4& = 0 \\[5pt] - \sqrt{8-2x} & = -4 \\[5pt] \sqrt{8-2x} & = 4 \\[5pt] \big(\sqrt{8-2x}\big)^2 & = 4^2 \\[5pt] 8-2x & = 16\\[5pt] -2x & =8 \\[5pt] x & = -4 \end{align*}

Finally, we must check the answer by substituting it back into the initial equation:

\begin{align*} - \sqrt{8-2(-4)} +4 & = 0 \\[5pt] - \sqrt{8+8} +4 & = 0 \\[5pt] -\sqrt{16}+4 & =0 \\[5pt] -4 +4 &= 0\\[5pt] -4+4 &= 0\\[5pt] 0 &= 0 \quad {\color{green}\checkmark} \end{align*}

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\textrm{$- 4$}}.$

exampleAnswers.title: Finding a Transformed Square Root Function Given Some Properties

question.text:
Let $f(x)=a\sqrt{2x+b}+c.$ Now consider the following properties of$f(x)\mathbin{:}$

  • The domain of $f(x)$ is $x \in \left[ 4,\infty\right).$

  • The range is $f(x) \in [-1,\infty).$

  • The point $(6,3)$ lies on the graph of $y=f(x).$
question.explanation:
Let's consider each property in turn.

  • The domain of $f(x)=a\sqrt{2x+b}+c\,$ is determined by the following inequality: \begin{align*} 2x+b &\ge 0 \\[5pt] 2x &\ge -b \\[5pt] x &\ge -\dfrac{b}{2} \end{align*} We are given that the domain is $x\in \left[4, \infty\right),$ which is equivalent to $x\ge 4.$ Hence, we obtain \[ -\dfrac{b}{2}=4 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad b=-8. \]

  • Since the range is unbounded on the right-hand side, we know that $a>0.$ Furthermore, since we are given that the lowest point in the range is $-1,$ we must have \begin{align*} \underbrace{a\sqrt{2x-8}}_{\geq 0}+c \ge -1. \end{align*} This means that $c=-1.$

  • Finally, since the point $(6,3)$ lies on the graph of $y=f(x),$ we have \begin{align*} f(6) & = 3\\[5pt] a\sqrt{2(6)-8}-1 & = 3 \\[5pt] 2a -1 & = 3\\[5pt] a &=2. \end{align*}

Therefore, our function is $f(x)=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{2\sqrt{2x-8}-1}.$

example.title: Finding a Transformed Square Root Function Given Some Properties

question.text:
Let $f(x)=a\sqrt{b-3x}.$ Now consider the following properties of $f(x)\mathbin{:}$

  • The domain of $f(x)$ is $x\in (-\infty, 1].$

  • The point $(-11,-24)$ lies on the graph of $y=f(x).$

Find the value of $a+b.$
question.explanation:
Let's consider each property in turn.

  • The domain of $f(x)=a\sqrt{b-3x}\,$ is determined by the following inequality: \begin{align*} b-3x &\ge 0 \\[3pt] -3x &\ge -b \\[3pt] x &\le \dfrac{b}{3} \end{align*} We are given that the domain is $x\in (-\infty, 1],$ which is equivalent to $x\leq 1.$ Hence, we obtain \[ \dfrac{b}{3}=1 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad b=3. \]

  • Since the point $(-11,-24)$ lies on the graph of $y=f(x),$ we have \begin{align*} f(-11) &=a\sqrt{3-3\cdot(-11)} \\[3pt] -24 &=6a \\[3pt] a&=-4. \end{align*}

Therefore, our function is $f(x)=-4\sqrt{3-3x}$ and

\[ a+b = -4 + 3 = -1. \]
